description: A position scale's padding is read from `config.scale`, and two of its entries were not read at all. Upstream resolves the three paddings in order, the whole `padding` first: `if (isContinuousToContinuous(scaleType)) { if (scaleConfig.continuousPadding !== undefined) return scaleConfig.continuousPadding; ... return barConfig.continuousBandSize; } if (scaleType === ScaleType.POINT) return scaleConfig.pointPadding;`, and then the outer half of a band, `if (scaleType === ScaleType.BAND) return getFirstDefined(bandPaddingOuter, paddingInner / 2)`. This compiler began each of those chains one link late: it went straight to `config.bar.continuousBandSize` without asking `continuousPadding`, and it always halved the inner padding without asking `bandPaddingOuter`, so a theme that padded its scales was answered with the built-in number instead. The first row is a band scale whose ends the theme widens, where the outer padding is the theme's 0.4 and not half of the bar's 0.1; its `y` shows that `continuousPadding` reaches a continuous scale on either axis. The second row is the same band with a stated `padding`, which settles both ends at once and outranks the theme, so it must stay a lone `padding` with no inner or outer beside it. The third row is a point scale, which `continuousPadding` never reaches because a point scale is not continuous-to-continuous, so it keeps `pointPadding` and must not change. The fourth row is a plain line, to show the theme's padding is not a bar's affair but every continuous position scale's. The fifth row is a bar against a continuous dimension, where the theme's `continuousPadding` outranks `config.bar.continuousBandSize` because upstream returns it before ever looking at the bar block. The sixth row states `paddingOuter` on the scale itself, which outranks the theme in turn.
